name: bright-cn/Etsy-dataset-sample
what_it_holds: A 1,001-row sample of Etsy product listings (price, title, category fields) extracted via the commercial Bright Data (formerly Luminati) scraping API, published as a marketing sample across several Bright Data locale repos (Chinese, Korean, Japanese, German, English variants of the same repo).
why_useful: Demonstrates a working commercial scraping method for marketplace listing/pricing data (Etsy as a discretionary small-ticket consumer-spend proxy); the committed sample itself is too small (1,001 rows, single pull, no dates) to be a time series, so only the method is worth noting.
themes: Gig-economy and platform-economy datasets (Uber/DoorDash/Etsy/Upwork public data) used as cross-platform consumer-behaviour reads
why_all: Demonstrates a working commercial scraping method for marketplace listing/pricing data (Etsy as a discretionary small-ticket consumer-spend proxy); the committed sample itself is too small (1,001 rows, single pull, no dates) to be a time series, so only the method is worth noting.

Demonstrates that Etsy listing-level data (price points, category mix) is scrapeable via a commercial vendor API and gives a small live sample, but the committed sample is tiny (1,001 rows, one-time pull) and the real product is a paid API, not an open dataset — marginal value as a pointer to a possible paid acquisition method for Etsy seller/price data as a small-business consumer-spend proxy.

name: api-evangelist/fiverr
what_it_holds: A written third-party profile/description of Fiverr's public API surface (no data files, no committed dataset, no working scraper) — part of a large 'API Evangelist' series profiling gig/marketplace companies (also found: taskrabbit, instawork, helpling, zego, work-market, syft, shiftsmart, zolvers, zehitomo, stride-health, and dozens more under the gig-economy topic).
why_useful: Marginal at best: no data or method, just descriptive text about each platform's API. Listed only because the series maps which gig platforms expose any public API surface at all, which could point a future scout toward an actual client/SDK repo if one exists for a given platform.

name: uber-trip-data
what_it_holds: CC0-licensed repo hosting Uber 2015 NYC trip data plus derived files: uber-data-2015.csv, uber-data-cleaned.csv, uber_merged.csv, aggregated_uber_pickup_borough.csv (borough-level daily aggregates), city_total_data.csv, weather_dict.csv (merged weather covariates), and a collision/casualty aggregate file, analysed in a Final Report.Rmd.
why_useful: Borough-level daily Uber pickup aggregates merged with weather is a usable template for a mobility-vs-weather cross-check, but the underlying trip data is the same stale 2015 NYC vintage as the FiveThirtyEight release, just pre-aggregated and CC0-licensed (easier reuse than the original TLC data).

name: Instacart Market Basket Analysis dataset (many GitHub mirrors/analyses, e.g. tstreamDOTh/Instacart-Market-Basket-Analysis, TheArc21/Instacart-market-basket-analysis)
what_it_holds: Instacart's public release (hosted on Kaggle, mirrored/discussed in dozens of GitHub repos) of 3M+ grocery orders from 200K+ users: order sequences, product/aisle/department info, order-day-of-week and hour-of-day timing, reorder flags. Original release circa 2017, static (no ongoing refresh).
why_useful: A large, real gig/on-demand-grocery order-timing dataset that could serve as a methodological analogue for modeling booking-time-of-day / day-of-week seasonality patterns relevant to STR booking behavior, and as a general on-demand-platform consumer-behavior reference; not Airbnb-specific and not time-extendable past ~2017.
license: Instacart's own Kaggle competition terms (non-commercial research use)
last_activity: static since original release; GitHub mirrors updated through 2026 (re-analyses only, not new data)

name: HotelRec
what_it_holds: ~50 million TripAdvisor hotel reviews (largest public hotel-review dataset per the authors, vs 0.9M in prior academic sets). Each review has hotel URL, reviewer username, date, overall rating, title, text, and sub-ratings (sleep quality, value, rooms, service, cleanliness, location). International coverage (sample shows Italian hotels; likely global given TripAdvisor's footprint). Actual data is not committed to the repo -- hosted on a SWITCHdrive link, restricted to academic research use only. Cites Antognini & Faltings, LREC 2020. Repo itself: 17 commits, README + download pointer.
why_useful: By far the largest and longest-running TripAdvisor review corpus found. A review-velocity / sub-rating time series built from this (filtered to years with real dates, cross-referenced to ABNB peer-set cities) could proxy hotel demand momentum and sentiment ahead of MAR/HLT RevPAR releases -- addresses gap #8 (hotel supply/demand) indirectly via review flow as a leading indicator, and gap #20 partially (party-size/length-of-stay not present but trip-type sub-ratings sometimes are). Academic-only license limits direct commercial reuse but fine for an internal model.
license: Academic research only (non-commercial); no open-source license stated for the download itself
time_coverage: Reviews with dates as early as ~2010 in samples shown; full range not confirmed
themes: TripAdvisor datasets: hotel/vacation-rental reviews, review velocity, TripAdvisor rentals, scraper repos

TripAdvisor review-volume-and-rating time series across a huge global hotel panel is a competitor/adjacent-supply engagement proxy (gap #9, and loosely gap #5 engagement signals) analogous to how Inside Airbnb reviews are used as a stays-index kernel for ABNB nights; review dates could be aggregated into a monthly hotel-demand pulse by market if the gated download is obtained.
